From 0–2 to Champs: Spindles UPL Inaugural Season Recap

The season began with two matches, two losses and zero goals.

It ended with Spindles United lifting the first championship trophy in Upstate Premier League history.

One year after winning the CDSL, Spindles stepped into a new league and answered a new challenge with the same result. The club finished first in the regular season, won both playoff matches without conceding and closed its inaugural UPL campaign as champions.

Across the regular season and playoffs, Spindles went 7–2–3, scored 22 goals, conceded 10 and recorded five clean sheets. Thirty players made an appearance, but the defining feature of the season was not any single number. It was the response whenever the campaign threatened to slip away.

Their rise was far from straightforward.

Over 10 regular-season matchweeks, Spindles moved from fourth to fifth, climbed as high as second, dropped back to fourth and entered the final matchweek in third. Only on the final day did they reach the top.

A new league for Upstate

The Upstate Premier League launched in 2026 with six community-based clubs representing Albany, Rensselaer, Saratoga and Schenectady counties: Spindles United, Collar City FC, Mohawk City FC, Patroon United, Sacandaga Lakers SC and United Soccer Group.

The league was created to raise the standard of organized amateur soccer in the Capital Region, pairing competitive 90-minute matches with local club identities, home grounds and community support. Each team played 10 regular-season matches—five home and five away—with the top four advancing to a 1-vs.-4, 2-vs.-3 playoff format.

The first season quickly became competitive. No club ran away with the table, and the results showed a race that changed almost every week.

Spindles experienced more of that movement than anyone.

A difficult introduction

Spindles’ first UPL match came May 17 against Mohawk City FC at Union College. The teams traded possession and half-chances before Mohawk turned a Spindles corner into a decisive counterattack in the 22nd minute. A late red card to debutant Nico Faretta left Spindles with 10 men, and the club’s first UPL appearance ended in a 1–0 defeat.

Elsewhere on opening weekend, Collar City defeated USG 4–1 and Patroon beat Sacandaga 3–1. Collar City took the first spot at the top of the table, followed by Patroon and Mohawk. Spindles sat fourth.

Five days later, the attack again came up empty. Spindles created opportunities against Collar City but were punished by a 75th-minute counterattack in another 1–0 road loss.

Collar City moved to 2–0 with the victory. Patroon also remained perfect by winning 2–1 at Mohawk, while Sacandaga collected its first points against USG. Spindles fell to fifth, ahead of USG only on goal difference.

Two matches. Two defeats. No goals.

For a team accustomed to competing for trophies, it was an unfamiliar position. The response arrived in one of the season’s most memorable matches.

Nine men and the first turning point

More than 150 supporters attended the first competitive match at Waterford-Halfmoon High School on May 29. David Kankam scored the first UPL goal in club history after Anders Trestick carried the ball 40 yards and found him at the far post.

Then the match turned chaotic.

Two second-half red cards reduced Spindles to nine players. With no substitute goalkeeper available, captain Marcos Lopez stepped into the net. Patroon attacked relentlessly, but Spindles protected the lead through a complete defensive effort and secured a remarkable 1–0 victory.

The result handed Patroon its first loss, but the rest of Matchweek 3 demonstrated how unpredictable the league had already become. Sacandaga won at previously unbeaten Collar City, while USG responded to its 0–2 start by defeating Mohawk 5–1.

After three weeks, Collar City, Patroon and Sacandaga each had six points. USG, Spindles and Mohawk each had three. Goal difference left Spindles fifth, but only one victory separated the entire league.

The season had changed.

Climbing into contention

Spindles followed their first victory with another 1–0 home win, this time against United Soccer Group. John Locicero converted an 18th-minute penalty—his 20th career goal for the club—and the defense produced its second consecutive clean sheet. The night also featured the club’s first live match broadcast.

Patroon defeated Collar City in the same matchweek to take sole possession of first place. Mohawk beat Sacandaga, leaving four clubs level on six points behind the leader.

Among them, Spindles had the best goal difference after Collar City. The back-to-back clean sheets lifted the club from fifth to third.

A week later in Galway, Spindles showed they could win a very different kind of game.

Zeidane Adjei opened the scoring against the Sacandaga Lakers with a spectacular strike from approximately 30 yards. Anders Trestick restored the lead in the 77th minute after Sacandaga had equalized, only for the Lakers to level again four minutes later.

With the match approaching its conclusion, Frankie Palumbo stepped over a free kick outside the box and curled it into the bottom corner. His 88th-minute winner completed a dramatic 3–2 victory, giving Spindles three consecutive wins and their first UPL road victory.

Mohawk also won in Matchweek 5, beating Collar City 3–1, while Patroon and USG drew 2–2. Those results left Patroon first with 10 points and Spindles second with nine. Mohawk also had nine but trailed Spindles on goal difference.

From fifth after Matchweek 3, Spindles had climbed to second by the halfway point.

Mohawk changes the table

Momentum stalled against Mohawk City on June 19. Adjei put Spindles ahead in the 51st minute, but the visitors scored twice in six minutes to complete a comeback and hand the club its first home defeat.

The result did more than end Spindles’ winning streak.

With Patroon held to a 1–1 draw by Sacandaga and Collar City defeating USG, Mohawk jumped from third to first. Patroon fell to second, Collar City rose to third and Spindles dropped from second to fourth.

Four clubs were now separated by three points.

That loss would be Spindles’ last of the season.

Against Collar City on June 28, Spindles fell behind after eight minutes but responded almost immediately. Trestick’s cross found Matt Rabadi, who controlled the ball and finished from a difficult angle for his first UPL goal. Although Spindles created chances to take all three points, the teams settled for a 1–1 draw.

Around the league, Patroon won a seven-goal match against Mohawk, 4–3, and USG produced the season’s largest scoreline with an 8–0 victory over Sacandaga.

Patroon returned to first. Mohawk remained second, while Collar City stayed ahead of Spindles on goal difference. With three matches remaining, Spindles were fourth—inside the playoffs, but only three points ahead of fifth-place USG.

Trestick takes over

Spindles traveled to league-leading Patroon United on July 12 and needed only 17 seconds to score.

An aggressive press forced a poor pass from the Patroon goalkeeper directly to Anders Trestick. His first-time finish was the fastest goal in club history.

Patroon eventually equalized, but the final 10 minutes belonged entirely to Spindles. Trestick scored in the 80th minute, struck again three minutes later to complete his second career Spindles hat trick, and watched Ryan Breen cap the performance with a powerful 25-yard finish.

The emphatic 4–1 road victory transformed the table again.

Sacandaga defeated Collar City 3–1, while USG won 2–1 at Mohawk. Patroon held onto first with 14 points, but Spindles moved back to second with 13. Mohawk fell to third, and USG climbed into the fourth and final playoff position.

With every club sitting between 10 and 14 points, nobody had been eliminated.

Five days later, Spindles appeared headed for another important win after goals from Trestick and Lopez produced a 2–0 halftime advantage over USG. The hosts responded with two goals during a frantic final stretch, forcing Spindles to leave Afrim’s Sports Park with a 2–2 draw.

Dominic Whalen earned Man of the Match honors for his defensive performance, but the dropped points sent Spindles back down to third.

Mohawk’s late 2–1 victory over Sacandaga moved it level with Patroon on 15 points. Patroon’s draw against Collar City left the two clubs separated only by goal difference. Spindles followed with 14, while USG and Collar City were level on 11.

Every playoff seed would be determined on the final weekend.

Five goals and first place

Spindles entered Matchweek 10 in third place, one point behind both Patroon and Mohawk.

Mohawk played first, drawing 1–1 with Collar City on July 24. The result moved Mohawk to 16 points but gave Spindles an opening.

Two days later, everything came together in Waterford.

Rabadi opened the scoring against Sacandaga in the 15th minute. Breen doubled the lead after Spindles’ pressure forced a goalkeeper error, and Rabadi added his second four minutes later.

Trestick made it four following a sweeping pass from Locicero, and Adjei completed the scoring in the 89th minute.

The 5–0 victory was Spindles’ largest of the UPL season. It moved the club to 17 points and, temporarily, into first place.

The regular season came down to its final match: Patroon against USG.

A Patroon victory would have sent Spindles back to second. Instead, USG battled to a 3–3 draw. Patroon collected one point, reaching 16—one short of Spindles. The result also allowed USG to secure fourth place over Collar City on goal difference.

The scores were in and the seedings were settled.

Spindles had finished one point ahead of both Patroon and Mohawk. USG and Collar City were also separated by goal difference alone.

The road to first place had taken every matchweek:

Fourth. Fifth. Fifth. Third. Second. Fourth. Fourth. Second. Third. First.

Built for the postseason

The final table produced two semifinal matchups: No. 1 Spindles against No. 4 USG, followed by No. 2 Patroon against No. 3 Mohawk.

USG controlled possession early in the first semifinal, but Spindles punished two turnovers in transition. Rabadi scored from a Nico Faretta pass in the 22nd minute before Locicero finished a Trestick cutback 10 minutes later.

Ryan Taylor made several important saves after halftime, while Man of the Match Luca Grestini helped anchor a disciplined defensive performance. The 2–0 semifinal victory sent Spindles into a second consecutive league final.

Patroon and Mohawk then played for the other place in the championship match. Patroon won 2–1, setting up a final between the regular season’s top two teams.

Spindles and Patroon had split two very different regular-season meetings. Spindles survived with nine men to win 1–0 in May, then produced a dominant 4–1 road victory in July.

The third meeting would decide the first UPL championship.

Champions of Upstate

The final was played August 9 at the Christian Plumeri Sports Complex in Albany, in front of a UPL-record crowd of 286.

Spindles controlled the early possession but had to wait until the 35th minute for the breakthrough. Daniel Primeau delivered toward the back post, where Rabadi met the ball with a perfectly timed volley. It was his fifth goal of the season and his second playoff opener in as many matches.

Patroon increased its pressure after halftime. Spindles answered by continuing to play through it.

In the 51st minute, Faretta threaded a pass through the Patroon defense to Trestick. The forward moved the ball onto his left foot and finished through the goalkeeper to double the lead.

From there, Taylor and the back line protected the clean sheet. Captain Dan Crook led the resistance, repeatedly breaking up dangerous attacks and earning Man of the Match honors.

When the final whistle sounded, the score read Spindles United 2, Patroon United 0.

The regular-season champions had completed the double. Spindles were also the first club to lift the UPL trophy, doing so before the largest recorded crowd of the league’s inaugural season.

The numbers behind the title

Trestick produced the most complete attacking season in the squad. He started 11 of 12 matches and finished with seven goals and four assists, giving him 11 direct goal contributions. His season included the fastest goal in club history, a hat trick against Patroon and the goal that secured the championship.

Rabadi delivered five goals in only eight appearances. Three came during the final three matches, including the opening goals in both the semifinal and final. He also led the squad with two Man of the Match awards.

Adjei contributed three goals in six appearances, while Locicero finished with two goals and three assists across all 12 matches. Breen added two goals, and Kankam, Palumbo and Lopez scored once apiece. Primeau and Faretta each supplied two assists, including one in the championship match.

At the other end, Spindles recorded five clean sheets. The final three matches—a 5–0 regular-season finale, a 2–0 semifinal and a 2–0 final—produced a combined score of 9–0.

The statistics tell the story of a balanced champion. The league table tells the story of persistence.

Spindles began their new era with two losses and fell as low as fifth. They climbed to second, dropped back to fourth, returned to second, slipped to third and finally reached first on the final day.

When the pressure was greatest, they produced three consecutive clean sheets and their most complete football of the year.

Different league. New opponents. Ten unpredictable matchweeks. First place. Another trophy.

Spindles United entered 2026 as defending CDSL champions.

They left it as the first champions of the Upstate Premier League.
